Population increased in Cardiff

The estimated population of Cardiff in 2024 was 383,919 usual residents, a rise of 1.1% since 2023.

This meant that Cardiff's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Cardiff increased by 6.7%.

Over this slightly longer period, Cardiff was also among the 10% fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Cardiff

The average (median) age rose to 34.4 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Cardiff has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Cardiff is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Cardiff's population of 383,919 usual residents was made up of:

  • 67,001 people aged 0 to 15 years, (17.5%)
  • 260,984 people aged 16 to 64 years, (68%)
  • 55,934 people aged 65 years and over, (14.6%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Cardiff has a higher proportion of people aged 16 to 64 years (68% compared with 62.8% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Cardiff, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Cardiff
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Cardiff, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 592 people (0.2%). In total, there were 3,566 births and 2,974 deaths in Cardiff.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 3,215 (-0.8%). There were 24,787 people entering the area and 28,002 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Cardiff's population of 6,845 (1.8%) as a result of 12,201 people entering the area and 5,356 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Cardiff was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Cardiff in mid-2023 is 379,739.

Within this, international migration was revised downwards by 1,033 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 2,764 people.

Overall, there was an revision downwards of 3,797 people.
